newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Senate sets vote dates on $2.9 bln bond deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Senate sets vote dates on $2.9 bln bond deal.

text.p: New Jersey Senate President Donald DiFrancesco set April 17 for the Legislature's first committee vote on a $2.9 billion pension bond deal, and four days later for a final vote, a legislative source said Friday.
"The concensus is, let's bring this thing to a vote at this point," Rae Hutton, a spokesman for Senate Republicans, said in an interview.

Hutton said the Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee will vote next Thursday in the first legislative test of the measure, which has suffered in recent weeks from flagging support among lawmakers and skepticism from voters.
If passed by the committee, the full Senate would vote April 21.
The Assembly had planned to take up the bill on March 24, but cancelled a vote amid growing opposition in the upper chamber.

Gov. Christine Whitman wants to use proceeds of the bond issue to pay off the state's unfunded pension liabilities. As part of the plan, the state would free up $647 million of pension contributions this year and next to help balance the budget.

Lawmakers, including some key Republican allies of the governor, have balked at the size of the bond issue -- the largest ever suggested by the state -- and said the debt would reduce New Jersey's financial flexibility.
New Jersey in February picked Merrill Lynch & Co to underwrite the issue if the Legislature approves it.
